text: The David E. Rumelhart Prize for Contributions to the Theoretical Foundations of Human Cognition was established in 2001 in honor of cognitive scientist David Rumelhart to serve as an equivalent to a Nobel Prize in the field of cognitive science. It is awarded annually to an individual or collaborative team that makes a significant contemporary contribution to the theoretical foundations of human cognition. The prize is presented each year at the Cognitive Science Society meeting, where the recipient delivers a lecture and receives a $100,000 check; at the end of the ceremony, the next year's recipient is announced. The award is funded by the Robert J. Glushko and Pamela Samuelson Foundation. The Rumelhart Prize committee operates independently of the Cognitive Science Society, although the society provides a large and engaged audience for the event. As of 2022, the selection committee included: Google AI, University of California, San Diego, Carnegie Mellon University, University College London, Yale University, Microsoft Research, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, New York University, Princeton University, Electronic Memories, Inc., Brandeis University, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, Bolt Beranek and Newman, Inc., University of Washington, Wayne State University, Duke University, Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology, University of Leipzig, Emory University, University of Edinburgh, University of Oxford, and University of Toronto.
